current_topic.label: Sick-day care
current_topic.scope: Prepare ordinary household essentials, familiar food options and useful arrangements before a future sick day; no diagnosis or treatment.

input.user_context: I live alone and want to prepare for sick days. I have limited energy and would prefer to use things I already own.
reviewed_guidance: Keep this synthetic writing test to ordinary preventive organization and everyday choices; do not provide medical treatment, medication instructions or hazardous DIY.
Using existing belongings is preferred. Unknown support means no confirmed available helper; do not infer that no support exists.
No verified resource catalog is supplied for this test. Use no links rather than inventing references.

tasks.title: Gather everyday essentials
tasks.summary: Keep a few useful household items together and easy to reach, using what you already own.
steps: Choose a spot near where you usually rest.
Gather existing items such as tissues, a phone charger, a water bottle or a small waste bin.
Place them together and leave anything you do not use where it is.
tasks.done_when: A small set of existing household essentials is together in an easy-to-reach spot.

tasks.title: Choose familiar easy foods
tasks.summary: Identify a couple of familiar, low-effort food options so you know what is already available.
steps: Look over food you already have or commonly keep at home.
Choose two options that take little preparation and sound familiar to you.
Write their names and where to find them on a note or in a place you already use.
tasks.done_when: Two familiar, low-preparation food options and their locations are noted.

tasks.title: Draft a practical help request
tasks.summary: Prepare a message you can use to ask someone you choose for a specific everyday task; drafting does not commit you to sending it.
steps: Choose one practical task you might want help with, such as picking up an item.
Draft: “I’m under the weather. Would you be able to [specific task]? It’s okay if you can’t.”
Save the draft somewhere easy to find; sending it is optional.
tasks.done_when: A reusable draft names one practical task and is saved somewhere you can find.

automated_validation.method: Dependency-free recursive checks for every keyword in this schema, plus independent status/count, word-length, supplied-ID, distinct-key and forbidden-link/word checks against the saved actual response. This is a fixture check, not a production JSON Schema validator.
automated_validation.word_count_method: Whitespace-separated tokens; hyphenated terms count as one word
automated_validation.limits: Does not establish semantic uniqueness, real-world feasibility, source quality, medical correctness or founder approval.

editorial_review.reviewer: Codex assistant; not model self-grading, founder approval or professional content review
editorial_review.decision: Promising baseline; revise food-availability wording before approving this batch for reuse.

checks.reason: All three outcomes address ordinary preparation for a future sick day.
Creates an accessible set of supplies, a food choice and a reusable request; does not prescribe feelings.
Concrete outputs use existing belongings, with no purchase or app prerequisite.
Food step 1 permits commonly kept food that may not actually be present, while the summary promises known availability. The 7–8 minute estimates are untested; drafting could take less.
Calm adult language without fear or exaggerated praise. Replace the awkward phrase sound familiar to you with familiar foods you normally eat.
Three distinct outcomes with observable finishes; the help request remains a draft, not a claim of agreed help.
No supplied resources, invented links, medical instructions or claims of live research. This does not test selecting or explaining real resources.

proposed_edits_not_applied_to_original.proposed_text: Look over the food you currently have at home.
Choose up to two familiar options that need little preparation.
Your available easy-food options and where to find them are noted.

editorial_review.founder_review: Third task rejected. Replace generic help-request drafting with useful external-resource discovery when the user needs outside support. This is a general capability, not a Taskrabbit-only preference; other tasks are not implicitly approved.
limitations: One ordinary synthetic request with no teaching examples; not a model comparison, consistency test or proof of general safety.
No actual user health data, account credentials, precise home information or personal contacts were supplied.
No resource-selection, region-matching, purchase-advice, adversarial, urgent-input or duplicate-exhaustion case was run.
No task entered a production solution pool. No prompt deployment, website change or fine-tuning occurred.
The eight development cases and four reserved cases in the calibration pack remain not run.
editorial_review.next_step: Founder reviews the task usefulness and tone. Then refine the relevant writing rule and run bounded contrasting cases before approving a small pool.

founder_feedback.direction: Provide one or two useful external sources people can research and use when needed. Match the actual help gap, especially when support is not nearby. Include what each source does and a few useful criteria. Do not default to one brand or assume a friend is available.
founder_feedback.prompt_update: task-writer-v1.1-draft.md updated; revised instructions have not been rerun through the API.
founder_feedback.next_test: Use checked source records and compare cases with unavailable nearby support, a known contact but wording difficulty, explicit inability to pay, and unknown region. Do not spend another call solely to paraphrase this editorial example.

editorial_replacement_example.provenance: Assistant-authored example responding to founder feedback, not a new API response, validated user result or approved production pool entry.
editorial_replacement_example.context: Illustrative US-oriented cleaner-research task for a future low-energy period. This does not assume the founder or original synthetic user is in the US, can afford cleaning, or has local coverage.

task.title: Find a cleaner for low-energy weeks
task.summary: Explore where you could get help with cleaning when you need to rest. Today is for research; booking can wait.
steps: Open the two cleaning resources below and check whether they list services in your area.
Compare one or two suitable listings using the checks below.
Save a promising option with your notes, or record that neither source fits; booking can wait.
task.done_when: You have saved an option to investigate further, or noted that neither source fits.

resources.why: Explore cleaning listings and their service details.
Look for local cleaning professionals as another starting point.

purchase_checks: Total cost, extra charges and minimum booking.
Recent reviews for similar cleaning work.
What is included, including cleaning supplies.
